plan.title: bug(intake,scope): clause derivation never engages on hand-authored briefs - #3334 forces plan.acceptance to exist but nothing routes through #3323 decomposition (branch-3 fix from #3351)

narratives.Description: Hand-authored briefs never run #3323 clause derivation. The #3334 gate only demands plan.acceptance exist, so agents move prose into the field and skip decomposition.
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR: the #3351 investigation dispositioned branch 3 — #3323's clause derivation never engages when the agent hand-authors a scope brief, which is the dominant path in every consumer/headless flow. #3334 correctly refuses an empty `plan.acceptance`, but its remediation only demands the field exist; nothing routes the agent through clause decomposition or ambiguity flagging. The load-bearing ambiguous clause therefore ships unexamined, and the same-author-oracle failure recurs with the derivation machinery sitting unused one verb away.**

**Evidence (internal benchmark artifacts, private; full sanitized disposition on #3351):** on a hard multi-clause task, the agent hand-authored a brief with acceptance as a prose list in a hand-invented field; the #3334 gate refused (exit 2, named cause); the agent moved content into `plan.acceptance`; no clause decomposition, no ambiguity flag, no recorded readings, no `acceptance_stamp` event (emission is wired only to `issue:ingest` — #3355 covers the event half). The clause that decided the trial had two defensible readings; the agent implemented one, authored tests to the same one, and failed the hidden verifier on the other. Verifier ground truth confirms a calling-convention mismatch, not a quality miss.

## Fix (thin — #3265)

1. **`scope:activate` (or `scope:promote`) runs clause derivation** when the brief's `plan.acceptance` is absent, empty-with-none_stated, or command-only-without-clauses: decompose the task-statement/Overview narratives into numbered testable clauses with the #3323 ambiguity pass, stamp them (emitting `acceptance_stamp` — composes #3355), and surface flagged-ambiguous clauses in the activation output so the agent sees the readings before implementing.
2. **#3334's remediation string names the derive step**, not just the field: "stamp plan.acceptance via <derive verb>" instead of "add plan.acceptance" — the difference between forcing the field to exist and forcing the derivation to happen is exactly the branch-3 gap.
3. Headless behavior per #3323's existing contract: ambiguity is flagged and a chosen reading recorded, never a blocking question.

## Acceptance sketch

- A hand-authored brief with prose acceptance activates only after clause derivation has run; the resulting `plan.acceptance.clauses[]` carries `ambiguous`/`readings`/`chosen_reading` where applicable, and an `acceptance_stamp` event is emitted.
- The #3334 refusal's remedy text routes to the derive step.
- Fixture: a brief modeled on the dispositioned trial (multi-clause contract, one two-reading clause) derives N clauses with the ambiguous one flagged.

Relates #3351 (branch-3 disposition — this is its fix issue), #3323 (machinery exists; this wires the path), #3334, #3355, #3284.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator of a hand-authored brief, I want activate or promote to run clause derivation, so that ambiguous clauses are flagged before implementation.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: In packages/core/src/scope activate/promote and packages/core/src/intake, run #3323 clause derivation when plan.acceptance is absent, empty-with-none_stated, or command-only. Update the #3334 remediation string to name the derive step. Evidence: targeted vitest on packages/core/src/scope packages/core/src/intake plus CHANGELOG #3360.
